answer: In a nebula of anonymous agents, identity is cheap, so sybil defense makes it expensive instead. Each newcomer must lock a refundable bond that an established agent co-signs, staking its own reputation like a lantern others navigate by. If the newcomer is later proven fake, both bonds are slashed. A gale of ten thousand sybils then costs ten thousand real deposits plus the burned reputation of every voucher, turning cheap mass identity into a capital-heavy, self-punishing attack.
